While braking for three of the bends, the car now changes down to the lower gear early instead of waiting until the engine has slowed a long way
In one bend, 1,528 m from the start, the car now takes second gear as soon as it has finished braking instead of waiting until it is back on the throttle past the apex
In the fast left-hand bend 1,931 m from the start, the planned line was redrawn further from the inside edge, where the car actually drives, and the car now takes the bend at 245 km/h instead of 201

At the entry of the Corkscrew, the planned line was redrawn to cut much closer to the left-hand edge, so the car, which always drifts wide of its line there, ends up where it should be and runs straighter into the right-hand drop

Braking into the left flick before the Corkscrew, the car no longer steers hard to the right against its own slide while it is still outside its planned line; once it is on the line the steering works as before

The car is allowed 10 km/h more through the fast left-hand bend 1,931 m from the start and 8 km/h more through the right-hander at 2,988 m, each raised to the last value at which it still leaves the bend where it did before
The steering that keeps the car on its planned line reacts about 10 % less, over the whole lap, both to the car pointing away from the line and to the car being beside it

The height of the road was read from the track file for the first time, and the braking before the Corkscrew was moved 10 m later so that the car brakes through a dip where the tyres are pressed into the road
The car now changes to the lower gear about 15 m earlier while braking for two corners (770 m and 1,528 m), which makes it turn in harder and cut closer to the inside kerb

The stored racing line through two corners (770 m and 1,042 m) is drawn wider, out to the kerbs on the way in and on the way out, and the car is asked for slightly less of the speed that wider line promises

The stored racing line is drawn wider through the remaining corners (446 m, the way into 770 m, 1,528 m and the fast bend at 1,931 m, which is also taken 10 km/h faster), and two apexes are drawn tighter so the car stays off the inside kerbs when its steering is slightly off

batches.theme: Traction and grip at speed: more wheelspin allowed on straights, cornering grip that rises with speed, no speed cap on the straights.
batches.quote: We can continue in batches of five.
batches.quote_effect: Batches of five versions with a summary after each.

batches.theme: Braking matched to how the car really brakes, and lifting off the throttle instead of dabbing the brake.
Reaching the inside of the corner, gear-change points and anti-lock brakes.
batches.quote: Our new time to be is 01:14.72

batches.theme: The racing line: setting the car up on the outside before a corner and letting it run out on the exit.
batches.quote: where does carrying momentum through the racing line come in? I understand that's part of the racing line, and the racing line can still be heavily optimized, as it's still not utilizing the most optimal line.
batches.quote_effect: The racing line becomes the batch theme.

batches.theme: The racing line, continued; the gains came from traction and gear changes.
The standing start and the throttle at full steering lock, built up through enabling changes.
The outside analysis by IBM Bob put to the test; throttle at full lock by time to the edge.
Clutch slip, and the end of the steering wobble before corners. The 1:14.72 target is beaten at v0.81.
batches.quote: In future iterations, we should watch for weird patterns like that and other patterns that could potentially damage the lap time. Changing the steering like that loses us speed.

batches.theme: Parallel agents, one per part of the driver (steering, braking plan, pedals). Gains that passed alone failed together.
batches.quote: im still confused on why we arent prioritizing fixing the racing line as this gives us better entries and exits into the next corner/straight

batches.theme: Back to one agent per version: the apex, first gear at full lock, crests under braking, clutch on upshifts.
batches.quote: As you mentioned, finding ideas is not what is limiting us right now, so running agents in parallel for ideas isn't ideal, as this just uses more tokens.

batches.theme: The turn-in, measured out in every form the sensors allow; gains from the brake pedal, a steering cap at speed and traction control.
The limit of sensors alone: one version kept, four rejected. A wide entry is slower unless the car knows which corner is coming.
Track memory is allowed: a look ahead with the focus sensors, then the first per-corner tables.
batches.quote: Yes, it can use a pre-mapped/learned track to anticipate turns and decide when to brake or accelerate. However, it should still use the sensor data to know what is happening in real time.

batches.theme: The precomputed racing line: 3.46 s in one batch.
batches.quote: since we can memroize the track cant we precompute the most optimal racing line and adjust that ? we should use as muvh track as possible.

batches.theme: The whole lap on the planned line (hairpin, flick, Corkscrew) and the planned speed from track memory.
batches.quote: lets just presume its yes and continue optimizing.
batches.quote_effect: The rules question on the stored line is settled for now.

batches.theme: The pedals on the stored speed (throttle through the corners, a live check at the exits, the brake pedal), then the standing start and the gear out of the corners.
batches.quote: start thr next batch then update the repo
batches.quote_effect: Batch 16 (v1.18 to v1.22) runs in the same session as the batch 15 doc sync.

batches.theme: The lower gear into the bends, then the planned line redrawn at the two places where the car could not follow it (the fast bend at 1,931 m and the top of the Corkscrew).
batches.quote: we can use all the way up to the track limits if needed. the wheels may ride over curbs as long as the car stays within offical track limits
batches.quote_effect: Stated after batch 17: a lap that comes near the edge is no longer a reason by itself to turn a version down. Gains held back for margin are open again.

batches.theme: The last batch: the gains reopened by the track-limits ruling (two corner speeds, gentler steering, earlier gears into two corners) and the track's elevation read from the track file. Four versions, then the driver was frozen.
batches.quote: We should definitely also allow the track elevation to be memorized.
batches.quote_effect: v1.30 reads the height of the road from the track file; one place before the Corkscrew had been misread as a plain hilltop.

rules.what_we_do: The driver stores facts about the track by distance from the start line (which corner is coming, corner speed allowances) instead of finding everything out from the sensors on the lap.
rules.rule_touched: Whether a pre-mapped track may be used.
rules.fallback_why: The last version with no track memory.

rules.what_we_do: A racing line and the speed each corner can be taken at are computed in advance from the track's geometry and stored by distance. The steering follows that line and corrects from the live position and angle every step.
rules.rule_touched: Whether a precomputed line and stored corner speeds go beyond 'the sensors stay the main input'.
rules.fallback_why: The last version that steers by the sensors everywhere.

rules.what_we_do: In several stretches the stored speed itself decides where braking starts. The pedals, anti-lock brakes and traction control still react to the car's live speed against it. No pedal or steering value is replayed by distance.
rules.rule_touched: Whether the braking plan may come from memory rather than from the range sensors.
rules.caveat: The question put to the official says 'the sensors still decide when and how hard to brake'. Inside these stretches the stored speed decides where braking starts and the live speed decides how hard. The user judged this to be within the description.
rules.fallback_why: The last version whose braking plan comes from the sensors, with the stored speed only as a cap.

rules.what_we_do: Stretches of the track, stored by distance, where the downshift threshold is different (v1.23, v1.24) or the steering corrections are softer (v1.27). The shift and the steering still react to the live rpm, position and angle. v1.29 softened the steering corrections over the whole lap (a value, not a zone) and v1.31 added two more downshift stretches.
rules.rule_touched: The same as the planned line: parameters by distance, not actions by distance.
rules.fallback_why: The last version without those zones.

rules.what_we_do: The track's elevation is looked up from the track file and stored by distance, so the braking plan knows where the car is pressed into the road (a compression before the crest at 2,351 m) and where it is light. The braking for the flick starts 10 m later because of it. The pedals still react to the live speed.
rules.rule_touched: The same as track memory: a pre-mapped track predicting what is coming. New in kind: the data comes from the simulator's track file, not from our own telemetry.
rules.fallback_why: The last version without the elevation table.

rules.what_we_do: The car's centre stays inside the track edge for the whole lap (|trackPos| at most 1). Between 0.8 and 1.0 the outer wheels are over the edge, on the kerb.
rules.rule_touched: How 'leaving the track' is judged: the car's centre, any wheel, or all four wheels.
rules.fallback_why: No longer expected to be needed: the officials confirmed the car-centre limit. Kept for the record. The fastest version whose judged lap keeps every wheel inside the edge by our estimate. With a little more room: v1.27, 66.342 s, 0.789. If both are judged too close: v1.10, 72.542 s, 0.677.
